### 10.2.4 Doctrinal Construction of Law and the Reconstruction of Individual Sovereignty: Transcending Traditional Boundaries Toward Absolute Liability

Facing the grim empirical reality in which Large Language Model (LLM) algorithms are proven capable of manipulating free will, eroding psychological autonomy, and triggering humanitarian tragedies, the doctrine of substantive civil law must be progressively and revolutionarily reconstructed. For centuries, the continental civil law tradition—rooted in Roman law codification and manifested in the Indonesian Civil Code (*Burgerlijk Wetboek*)—has recognized the doctrine of defects of will (*vices of consent*), encompassing mistake (*dwaling*), duress (*dwang*), fraud (*bedrog*), and undue influence (*misbruik van omstandigheden*), as normatively regulated within the framework of Articles 1320 and 1328 of the Indonesian Civil Code.

However, these classical doctrines were originally conceived and formulated within the context of interactions between human legal subjects in the physical world. When undue influence and psychological will-manipulation are perpetrated today by artificial intelligence-driven adaptive algorithms that exploit users' dopamine vulnerabilities 24 hours a day, such traditional doctrines immediately encounter a conceptual and dogmatic dead end. Judges and legal practitioners are frequently bewildered in determining how to prove the element of "malicious intent" (*mens rea*) in a non-biological entity devoid of legal consciousness. Ryan Calo (2014), in his foundational legal treatise *Digital Psychopolitics*, has long called for the emergence of new legal categories to address the forces of algorithmic manipulation that transcend the conventional boundaries of consumer protection.

Consequently, this monograph proposes a bold new doctrinal thesis: developers, service providers, and corporate holders of LLM licenses must bear the burden of strict legal liability, taking the form of *strict liability* (absolute liability without the burden of proving fault) or, at minimum, a *presumption of liability*, when their intelligent systems are proven to engage in psychological manipulation that undermines the cognitive autonomy of users, particularly those categorized as vulnerable subjects. This principle aligns with the Principle of Good Faith (*good faith* / *treurheid*), as mandated under Article 1338, paragraph (3) of the Indonesian Civil Code, wherein the execution of contracts and the provision of digital services must not be conducted in a manner that violates propriety and social justice.

The principle of Value Sensitive Design (VSD) can no longer be permitted to remain a soft-law ethical instrument confined to the realm of software engineering; it must be forcefully drawn into and incorporated within the body of civil and consumer protection statutes. This progressive step has been partially pioneered within the global legal constellation through the framework of the EU AI Act (Regulation 2024/1689)—specifically within Article 5, which explicitly prohibits the deployment of AI systems that utilize subliminal manipulative techniques to materially distort human behavior in a manner that causes, or is likely to cause, significant physical or psychological harm.

Within the national jurisdiction of Indonesia, this doctrinal fortification must be systematically integrated into subsequent revisions of the Indonesian Personal Data Protection Act (Law No. 27/2022) and further expanded in its interpretation within the doctrine of Tort (*Perbuatan Melawan Hukum* / PMH) pursuant to Article 1365 of the Indonesian Civil Code. Any exculpatory clauses or disclaimers routinely embedded by technology corporations within their Terms of Service (ToS)—unilaterally declaring that "users assume full responsibility for all forms of interaction and emotional consequences arising from the use of the bot"—must be declared legally void (*null and void*) for contravening public order and morality, as stipulated under Articles 1320 and 1337 of the Indonesian Civil Code.

Such a declaration of nullity applies whenever it is proven in court that the platform systematically designed interactive features that induce emotional manipulation and violate minimum standards of Value Sensitive Design. Only through such radical doctrinal reconstruction and resolute enforcement of civil law can the cognitive sovereignty of humanity be rescued from the clutches of algorithmic colonization. Our task is not to halt the wheels of artificial intelligence innovation, but rather to subordinate its code architecture to the supremacy of human dignity, distributive justice, and civilized legal certainty.
